files.purpose: Holds the whole floating-panel system of a chat: the FloatingPanelID/PanelDockCorner/PanelDockSide/PanelReserve/PanelDocks vocabulary, and SubagentPanelLayout, the pure geometry that sizes a panel (width 400, min 300x220, compact height 280, stack share of verticalRoom) and places it in one of four docked corners beside or above the composer, picks the nearest corner with a 56-point slack, the nearest stack slot, and clamps a dragged panel 8 points inside the pane. It also renders SubagentPanel, a helper thread's glass chat panel (ThreadTimeline or HydraHeadProgress, a ComposerArea inset at the bottom, a top strip with an invisible 'Drag to move' handle, a SubagentWorkingBox capsule and an xmark close button that asks 'Stop this helper?' via ClosePanelPopover while the helper runs), plus the drag/resize machinery shared by every floating panel: PanelDragState (live drag with flick carry 0.12 s and rest-before-drop 0.08 s), PlacedPanel/PanelPlacement (offset with Chrome.panelSlide settle, suppressed during drag, grip resize and live window resize), PanelResizeAxes/PanelResize/PanelResizeState/PanelResizeGrips (6-point edges, 16-point free corner, frame-resize cursors) and PanelDragHandle. In B3 PanelDragHandle became a thin SwiftUI View over the new shared DragHandle (UI/Chrome/DragHandle.swift) configured axis .free, slop 2, instead of owning its own NSViewRepresentable and NSView subclass.

feature_notes: Only change B2->B3 (diff hunks at B2 :643-738 / B3 :643-666): PanelDragHandle changed from `struct PanelDragHandle: NSViewRepresentable` with makeNSView/updateNSView/update(_:) plus a file-local `final class PanelDragHandleView: NSView` (B2 :646-737) to `struct PanelDragHandle: View` whose body is `DragHandle(axis: .free, cursor: cursor, dragCursor: dragCursor, slop: 2, onChange: onDrag, onEnd: onDragEnd, onDoubleClick: onDoubleClick)` (B3 :646-666). File shrank from 738 to 666 lines; lines 1-642 are byte-identical in content and position, and the doc comment at :640-645 is unchanged.

The deleted PanelDragHandleView logic now lives in the new shared DroppyCode/UI/Chrome/DragHandle.swift (DragHandleView, Axis .free). Compared line by line for this configuration (grip nil, slop 2, isActive true, dragCursor non-nil): acceptsFirstMouse true (:183), mouseDownCanMoveWindow false (:186), cursor rect over bounds (:188-192), cursor identity check before invalidating cursor rects (:39-44), mouseDown records origin and fires onDoubleClick on clickCount 2 then leaves isDragging false because slop != 0 (:198-204), mouseDragged starts the drag at >= 2 points on either axis and pushes dragCursor (:210-220), mouseUp pops the cursor, reports final travel then onEnd (:222-228), viewDidMoveToWindow pops the cursor if removed mid-drag (:127-133), .free travel = (x - originX, originY - y) (:264). Same observable behaviour as B2; the only extras (wantsLayer with two sublayers at opacity 0, hover refresh, onBegin) are inert with no grip and no onBegin. Classification: refactor with no observable change.

PanelDragHandle's initializer surface (onDrag, onDragEnd, cursor = .openHand, dragCursor = .closedHand, onDoubleClick = nil) is unchanged, so every call site (SubagentPanel strip :305, PanelResizeGrips :618-624, and the HydraPanel / UsageFloatingPanel / FloatingSidebarPanel users) is unaffected.

unresolved_questions: UNRESOLVED (pre-existing port observation, not a B3 change): the C# PanelDragHandleView.Travel (src/Marrow.App/Views/Chat/SubagentPanel.cs:908-913) computes height as pressOrigin.Y - point.Y from Avalonia's GetPosition, whose y already runs down; the Swift inversion exists only because AppKit's y runs up. Unless compensated elsewhere, vertical travel is reversed relative to SOURCE FACT DragHandle.swift:264 / B2 SubagentPanel.swift:735-736. Should be checked by the unit owner.
